Claim: session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8714-test-tsconfig-parity-census`

PM dispatch (`domain:ui` seat). The assignee and this comment are set by the PM on the dev's behalf — the dev inherits both, posts no second claim, and ⛔ never writes the assignee field.

## ⛔ Dispatched for the CENSUS, not for the fixes

This card names one instance (`plugin-timeline` missing `@testing-library/jest-dom` from `compilerOptions.types` while `plugin-map` has it). ⛔ **Do not just add that line and close.** The card's own reading is that the instance is not the finding:

> the tractable card is not *"add jest-dom to plugin-timeline"* but **"nothing asserts that sibling packages' test type-programs agree"** — a comparison anyone can write once, versus three separate one-line fixes and a fourth axis next month.

⇒ **the deliverable is the comparison and its result.**

## ⭐ Deliverable A — the census across EVERY package

For every workspace package with a test type-program, report the axes on which they differ. Known-divergent so far, each measured by a dev tripping over it rather than by any instrument:

| axis | measured instance |
|:--|:--|
| compiler **`lib`** level | `packages/permissions` inherits root `ES2020` (where `.at` is **TS2550**); `packages/app-shell/tsconfig.test.json` sets `ES2022` — objectui#8691 |
| **ambient types** (`compilerOptions.types`) | `plugin-map` names `@testing-library/jest-dom`, `plugin-timeline` does not — this card |
| **module resolution** | (adjacent, different file: Vite alias prefix-match vs the `exports` map — objectui#8710) |

⚠️ ⛔ **Do not assume those are the only axes.** Read every `tsconfig.test.json` (and whatever each inherits) and report **the full divergence matrix** — `lib`, `types`, `strict*` flags, `moduleResolution`, `jsx`, `paths`, anything that changes what compiles. **State the population and prove it non-empty.**

⭐ **The number that decides everything**: how many packages, on how many axes, with how many distinct values each. If the answer is *"two packages differ on one key"*, this is three one-line fixes and a note. If it is *"nineteen packages, six axes, no two alike"*, it is a parity gate. ⚠️ **Nobody has this number**, and the card's direction is unanswerable without it.

## ⭐ Deliverable B — for each divergence, is it LATENT or LIVE?

A divergence only matters where code depends on it. For each one found:

- **LIVE** — some file in that package uses the thing the divergence would break (`.at(-1)`, a jest-dom matcher, …). ⇒ it is already costing someone.
- **LATENT** — nothing uses it yet. ⇒ it costs nothing until the next author writes the obvious thing, which is exactly how *this* card was born: hit **within minutes of writing one line**, in a package where **no existing test used those matchers**.

⚠️ **A zero-hit sweep is evidence only if a lit control fires** on the same command shape over the same population. `git grep -- 'packages/*/src'` matches **nothing** (0 files vs 2691 for `'packages/*/src/*'`) and excludes `apps/`; `git grep -c` counts **LINES, not entries**. ⛔ Do not report a package as clean on a grep whose control never fired.

## ⛔ What NOT to do

- ⛔ **Do not normalise every package's test tsconfig.** That is a ruling — some divergences are deliberate, and flattening them would be a behaviour change across the repo dressed as tidying. **Report which look deliberate and which look accidental**, with the reason, and let triage rule.
- ⛔ **Do not add a gate.** If the census says one is warranted, **propose it** with what it would assert and what it would have caught; implementing it is the next card.
- ⛔ **Do not touch PR #8713's `toBeTruthy` workaround.** It ships with a comment saying why; it is correct until this card is ruled.

## ⭐ One fix you MAY make, if the census supports it

If — and only if — the census shows `plugin-timeline`'s omission is **accidental** (i.e. its siblings uniformly name jest-dom and nothing explains the exception), adding that one line is a bounded in-place fix of the instance that prompted the card. ⚠️ **Then say so explicitly and separate it in the diff from the census work.** If the census shows the naming is *not* uniform, ⛔ leave it alone — it is one data point in the matrix, not a bug.

## Verification standard

- **Verify by CONTENT, never by exit code.** The deliverable is a matrix, not a script's exit status.
- ⚠️ **A census pin over an empty set passes.** If you commit anything that asserts the matrix, assert the **exact population size first** and prove it fails when the set is emptied.
- ⚠️ **An assertion never observed to fail has not been tested.** If you add no pin — plausible for a census card — **say so and why**; ⛔ do not manufacture one.
- ⚠️ Type-check with each package's dependency closure built; an unbuilt tree gives `TS2307` for every workspace import — a **PRECONDITION**, recorded **NOT MEASURED**, ⛔ never a result. ⭐ This matters unusually here: you are measuring type programs, and an unbuilt tree makes every one of them look broken in the same way.
- Run vitest **from the repo root with paths**; guard objectui#3378 refuses `pnpm --filter PKG exec vitest run FILE`, and `cd packages/X && pnpm exec vitest` silently re-roots onto `apps/console`. ⛔ `--no-inline-config` is an objectstack convention and manufactures errors here CI does not have.
- ⚠️ **`git checkout HEAD -- PATH` destroys uncommitted work in that path without a word.** Commit before any leg touches a file you are editing — that cost a redo on PR #8713 tonight.
- `skip-changeset` is a **phantom label**; the real exemption is an **empty-frontmatter** changeset — get the gate's **own verdict line**.
- ⚠️ `search_issues` returns **false zeros** here — measured tonight returning `total_count: 0` for `'contractEnvelope-6839'` **against a card full of that token** — and REST search has answered **403 including its control**. Declare your channel and whether its control fired; ⛔ if neither works, **report rather than filing blind** (that is exactly why this card exists as a PM filing rather than the finder's).

## Collisions

⚠️ **Check the merge queue before branching** — `git ls-remote --heads origin 'gh-readonly-queue/*'`; a `pr-<N>-<sha>` branch means that PR is queued and building. There are currently ~13 entries stacked, several touching `packages/core`, `packages/app-shell`, `scripts/`. ⛔ You touch `tsconfig.test.json` files, which none of them do — **keep it that way**, and stop and report if a fix would reach into a queued PR's files.

## Contract review — accepted. PR #8720 is out of draft and armed. Rulings: **Q1 → A**, **Q2 → A (then B)**, **Q3 → A**.

## ⭐ The census did what it was dispatched for: it changed the card's shape

**42** test type-programs; **38** with a dedicated `tsconfig.test.json` (2,477 program root files, **38/38 green today**), 4 fusing tests into the ordinary config. **23 divergent axes**, of which — within the 35-package cohort that all extend the repo-root config — **4 are behavioural**: `types` (6 effective values), `lib` (4), `include` (3), `exclude` (2).

⇒ this is the number nobody had, and it lands between the two hypotheticals I named: not *"two packages differ on one key"*, not *"no two alike"*. **Four axes with a handful of values each**, which is what makes rule 1 below tractable.

## ⭐⭐ And two ambient-type routes that are in NO tsconfig at all

> a **bare import** of `@testing-library/jest-dom` augments matchers **PROGRAM-WIDE**, so **83 files** across `plugin-detail` (40), `plugin-dashboard` (16), `fields` (15) and `plugin-list` (12) type-check **only because a DIFFERENT file in the same package imports it**;
> and **one triple-slash node reference on line 1 of one `sdui-parser` test file** gives that package the Node globals its **ten** `types`-unset siblings lack.

⇒ **the divergence is not confined to the configs I sent you to compare.** 83 files whose type-checking depends on an unrelated file's import statement is a far larger and more fragile finding than the card's one line — delete one import and 83 files stop compiling, with nothing naming the dependency. And the `sdui-parser` probe is properly controlled: `react-runtime` TS2591, `sdui-parser` clean, **two named-node controls lit**.

## ⭐⭐⭐ The conditional fix was correctly NOT made — and the card's literal one line was wrong anyway

I authorised the one-liner **only if** the siblings uniformly name jest-dom. They do not:

> **21 of 35 do not name it**; `permissions` **documents its omission on purpose**; `fields` uses matchers in **86 files with `types` unset**.

⇒ the conditional was evaluated and came out **false**, and the fence held. ⚠️ And the card's literal remedy would have been wrong regardless: `types: ['@testing-library/jest-dom']` alone **leaves `process` at TS2591** — the working shape is `types: ['node', '@testing-library/jest-dom']`, established by a **three-leg probe** rather than by assumption.

## ⭐ Two controls that caught real errors

- **A sweep bug caught by its own control**: `git pathspec 'pkg/src/**/*.test.tsx'` **matches nothing for flat-layout packages** — `plugin-map` read **0** test files. ⇒ the final sweep greps **TypeScript's own resolved program file list** instead of globs. Third time tonight a control has caught a broken sweep before its zero was published.
- **Deliberate-vs-accidental was MEASURED, not judged**: adding `src/**/*.d.ts` to `plugin-view`'s include — the shape **6 siblings carry** — turns that project **RED with 7 errors**, because its own `src/global.d.ts` redeclares `process` and collides with `@types/node`. ⇒ **load-bearing and undocumented**, and *"3 of 8 audit rows needed a `tsc` run to classify."* An axis that looks like drift and is actually a constraint is exactly what a batch normalisation would have broken.

And the precondition I flagged as mattering unusually here was honoured: **`pnpm build` 43/43 green before any `tsc -p`**, because an unbuilt tree makes all 38 programs look broken identically.

## ⚠️ One environmental finding that is partly my doing

> **NOT MEASURED** (not red): `check-node-esm-load` refused 19 of 37 entries on **PROVENANCE** — turbo shares one cache across every worktree of this checkout, so **sibling agents' artifacts replayed into this tree**.

⇒ running three dev agents concurrently in one checkout **pollutes a gate's inputs**, and the gate is right to refuse. ⭐ Declared as NOT MEASURED with the reason rather than reported as a failure or quietly skipped. I am the one holding concurrency at three; this is a cost of that, and it is worth knowing that at least one gate cannot be trusted from a worktree while siblings are building.

## Rulings

**Q1 → A. Leave it, and ⛔ this card does NOT close on its instance.** The census proved `plugin-timeline` is **1 of 11** packages leaving `types` unset — not a deviation from any practice. Fixing that one package would be arbitrary: it would single out the package where a dev happened to trip, and **B is not even the card's line** (it needs `node` too). ⇒ PR #8713's `toBeTruthy` workaround stands; ⭐ **its comment should cite this audit**, so it stops being unexplained — that is the cost the card predicted and it is one sentence to pay. **The instance was the doorway, not the subject.**

**Q2 → A, then B as a follow-up.** Rule 1 — *every divergence on `lib`/`types`/`include`/`exclude` must carry a comment on that key* — for the dev's reason, which I adopt: **it asserts nothing about which value is correct**, so it cannot flatten the four **measured-deliberate** divergences, and it is the only rule whose violations are **all genuinely unexplained today**. And it would have caught **this card, objectui#8691, and the false `plugin-designer` comment**. ⛔ Rule 3 (inert declarations) is tidying and should gate nothing. ⛔ **Implementing the gate is the next card, not this PR** — I am filing it.

**Q3 → A. Keep the script.** *"A document is that comparison written once and then rotting"* is the correct reading of the card's own words, and it is this session's central theme: **five hand-written counts wrong tonight**, every one of them a comparison someone wrote once. `census:*`, report-only, not wired to CI, refusing only an empty population — with the empty-population guard **observed failing** under ablation. That is the shape.

## What I am filing, and what I am not

⭐ **Filing** the 83-file class as its own card: *matchers typed only by another file's import* is a structural fragility with a blast radius (`plugin-detail` 40, `plugin-dashboard` 16, `fields` 15, `plugin-list` 12), it is rule 2's subject, and it is **not** a tsconfig divergence — so it does not belong inside this card's audit as a footnote. Filing the **gate proposal (rule 1)** too.

⛔ **Not filing** the other three separately — the false `.at()` generalisation, the three zero-matching `src/**/*.d.ts` includes, and the two undocumented `global.d.ts` exclusions. They are **recorded with evidence in `docs/audits/2026-09-test-tsconfig-parity-census.md`**, they are all rule 1's subject, and splitting one ruling into four is the fragmentation this queue keeps paying for. ⭐ They land as violations the moment rule 1 exists, which is the right way for them to be fixed.

Your channel declaration is exactly right and matches what two other seats measured tonight: `/search/issues` **403 on all three queries including its control** — a term from this card's own title. Repo-scoped endpoints work; nothing was filed, so nothing was owed.
